stories.title: WNC Closes on 23rd California-Focused Affordable Housing Fund
stories.excerpt: WNC & Associates, Inc. has closed on WNC Institutional Tax Credit Fund X California Series 23, L.P. The $66.3-million fund is the company’s 23rd consecutive California-focused multi-investor affordable housing fund for institutional investors. CA23 includes six new-construction affordable housing properties totaling 650 homes across Los Angeles, San Benito and San Diego counties, Financing from the fund will help four developers bring their projects to completion. All six properties will serve families and utilize 4% Low-Income Housing Tax Credits. “Closing CA23 is an important milestone for WNC as we celebrate our 55th year of operations” said Will Cooper Jr., president and CEO of WNC. “We are proud of our California roots and the role our home state has played in WNC’s growth into a national affordable housing organization.” The Irvine-based company has sponsored 41 California-focused funds and invested in 350 properties across 180 communities in the state, in addition to its national footprint. The post WNC Closes on 23rd California-Focused Affordable Housing Fund appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: WNC closed $66.3M California affordable fund (23rd consecutive), financing 650 units across LA, San Benito, San Diego
Six new-construction properties utilize 4% LIHTC; WNC has invested in 350 CA properties across 180 communities
Strong institutional demand for CA affordable housing equity despite rate environment and LIHTC market headwinds
stories.summary: WNC & Associates closed its 23rd consecutive California-focused multifamily affordable housing fund at $66.3 million, financing six new-construction properties totaling 650 units across Los Angeles, San Benito, and San Diego counties using 4% Low-Income Housing Tax Credits. The Irvine-based firm has now sponsored 41 California-focused funds investing in 350 properties. The closure signals ongoing institutional appetite for CA affordable housing despite broader market uncertainty.
stories.impact: Sustained LIHTC equity availability in California's major metros (LA, San Diego) and emerging secondary markets (San Benito) suggests development financing remains accessible for affordable projects, lowering cost of capital for mission-driven operators. However, reliance on 4% credits (not 9%) indicates moderating rents/lower-income targeting, signaling either market softness in affordability segments or regulatory pressure to prioritize deeper income levels in high-cost metros.

stories.title: Berkadia Secures $12M in LIHTC Equity for Michigan Housing Property
stories.excerpt: Berkadia secured financing for Lighthouse Ridge Apartments, a 52-unit garden-style multifamily property in South Haven, Michigan. Associate Director James Grande of Berkadia Affordable Housing led the Berkadia team in securing $12.4 million in LIHTC equity on behalf of the developer, Wallick Development, in partnership with Bogan Developments and Mno-Bmadsen. The deal marks Berkadia’s first closing with Wallick. “Lighthouse Ridge Apartments is a meaningful project for the South Haven market,” said Grande. “This investment supports the creation of new housing options that will benefit the broader community for years to come.” Once complete, the community will include 40 two-bedroom and 12 three-bedroom units housed in three buildings. It will also include a separate clubhouse, which will house the community space, management office, laundry room, fitness center and business center. Join the industry’s top multifamily decision-makers at Connect Apartments on September 22 in LA. Hear from the investors, developers, lenders, owners, and advisors shaping today’s apartment market through candid conversations, networking, and market insights. Register today at www.connectapts2026.com. The post Berkadia Secures $12M in LIHTC Equity for Michigan Housing Property appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Berkadia arranged $12.4M LIHTC equity for 52-unit garden-style property in South Haven, Michigan
Lighthouse Ridge Apartments includes 40 two-bed, 12 three-bed units with clubhouse and amenities in three buildings
First closing between Berkadia and Wallick Development signals emerging provider relationships in Midwest affordable market
stories.summary: Berkadia Affordable Housing secured $12.4 million in LIHTC equity financing for Lighthouse Ridge Apartments, a 52-unit garden-style community in South Haven, Michigan, developed by Wallick Development in partnership with Bogan Developments and Mno-Bmadsen. The property will deliver 40 two-bedroom and 12 three-bedroom units with shared amenities including clubhouse, fitness center, and business center. This represents Berkadia's first closing with Wallick.
stories.impact: Michigan affordable housing development (particularly secondary markets like South Haven) remains achievable with traditional LIHTC structures, suggesting modest but steady demand for workforce housing in Midwest markets. The garden-style typology and 52-unit scale indicate developers are building smaller, amenity-rich communities rather than larger urban projects, potentially reflecting lower land costs and labor availability in non-metro markets but also softer rent growth trajectories.

stories.title: Acadia Buys Mixed-Use Property on SoHo’s Greene Street for $60M
stories.excerpt: Acadia Realty Trust has snapped up a mixed-use property on SoHo’s Greene Street. The real estate investment trust (REIT) purchased two interconnected buildings at 69 Greene Street and 71-73 Greene Street from New York City-based property investment firm JSRE Acquisitions for a combined $60 million, according to city records made public Tuesday. The deal was completed in two separate transactions. Using the entity 69 Greene Owner, Acadia bought the five-story residential and retail building at 69 Greene Street for $29.4 million, while the REIT used the LLC 71-73 Greene Owner to acquire the five-story residential and retail property at 71-73 Greene Street for $30.6 million, records show. Streetwear boutique Amiri is currently a retail tenant at the base of the property. The properties last sold for $33 million in 2012. JSRE, which is affiliated with the billionaire Safra family, used similarly named entities in the transactions. Carlos Bertaco and Gina Sutt Malul signed the deals for JSRE, while Jason Blacksberg, executive vice president and chief legal officer at Acadia, signed for the buyer, according to records. It’s unclear who brokered the new deal. A spokesperson for Acadia did not immediately respond to a request for comment, while a spokesperson for JSRE could not be reached for comment. The deal represents Acadia’s continued interest in retail properties along Greene Street after buying the Givenchy-anchored retail condo at 92 and 94 Greene Street from Continental Ventures for $44 million in October 2024, as Commercial Observer previously reported. Also in SoHo, the REIT bought the Moschino-anchored retail condo at 73 Wooster Street for $25 million in January 2025. But Acadia seems focused on retail investments in general across New York City. In February, it acquired four storefronts along Madison Avenue on Manhattan’s Upper East Side from Naftali Group for a total of $20.7 million. bullets: Acadia Realty Trust acquired two SoHo mixed-use buildings (69 & 71-73 Greene Street) for $60M from JSRE Acquisitions
Properties last traded at $33M in 2012; current $60M price reflects 82% appreciation over 13 years
Five-story residential/retail mix with Amiri boutique tenant; Acadia using separate LLCs per property acquisition structure
stories.summary: Acadia Realty Trust purchased two interconnected mixed-use buildings at 69 Greene Street and 71-73 Greene Street in SoHo's core for a combined $60 million, acquiring the assets from NYC-based property firm JSRE Acquisitions (affiliated with the Safra family). The five-story buildings contain residential and retail space, with Amiri streetwear boutique anchoring the ground-floor retail. The properties last sold in 2012 for $33 million.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily development relevance; this is a REIT's acquisition of stabilized mixed-use assets in a trophy submarket. However, the $60M price for two small SoHo buildings underscores Manhattan's persistent scarcity premium and strong capital demand for well-located retail-residential hybrids, signaling that SoHo's tight residential supply and high retail rents continue to attract institutional capital away from ground-up development and toward existing stock.

stories.title: GAIA lands One-Year Extension on Williamsburg Multifamily Loan
stories.excerpt: GAIA Real Estate has secured an additional one-year extension of its $48-million loan with Raymond James Bank for 55 Hope, a 117-unit multifamily property in Williamsburg, Brooklyn. The extension pushes the loan’s maturity to August 2027. “We are pleased to continue our partnership with Raymond James at 55 Hope,” said Danny Fishman, CEO and co-founder, GAIA Real Estate. “We acquired the property at the height of the COVID-19 pandemic, amid significant uncertainty in New York, and have since increased net operating income significantly through active management and a long-term approach to value creation. This extension demonstrates our ability to identify opportunities across market cycles and position our investments for sustained performance in Brooklyn’s multifamily market.” Originally built as a pencil factory, 55 Hope was gut-renovated in 2012 into condo-style apartments. Since its inception, GAIA Real Estate has acquired more than 20,000 residential units and managed approximately $4 billion in assets. The post GAIA lands One-Year Extension on Williamsburg Multifamily Loan appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: GAIA Real Estate extended $48M Raymond James Bank loan on 117-unit Williamsburg property (55 Hope) to August 2027
Asset acquired during COVID-19 pandemic; GAIA increased NOI significantly through active management and long-term positioning
One-year extension demonstrates lender confidence and GAIA's value-creation track record in Brooklyn multifamily market
stories.summary: GAIA Real Estate secured a one-year extension on its $48 million loan from Raymond James Bank for 55 Hope, a 117-unit condo-style multifamily property in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, pushing maturity to August 2027. GAIA acquired the gut-renovated pencil factory (originally converted to condos in 2012) during the COVID-19 downturn and has since increased the property's NOI substantially through active management. The extension reflects lender confidence in the asset and GAIA's operational performance.
stories.impact: Lender willingness to extend at par on a stabilized Williamsburg value-add property signals confidence in Brooklyn's rental fundamentals and GAIA's execution, but the one-year (not multi-year) extension suggests Raymond James is cautious about committing longer-term amid rate uncertainty. For developers: this validates that acquiring pandemic-distressed multifamily in Williamsburg and improving operations remains viable, though refinance windows are tightening and lenders expect near-term rate clarity before offering longer extensions.

stories.title: Women’s Clothing Store Esti’s Takes 8K SF at 2263 Nostrand Avenue in Midwood
stories.excerpt: High-end women’s clothing store Esti’s is relocating to a new mixed-use development in Midwood, Brooklyn, Commercial Observer has learned. The longtime retailer’s 7,800-square-foot lease at 2263 Nostrand Avenue was signed on Tuesday. Asking rent for the 10-year deal was $65 per square foot. The retail space at the corner of Nostrand Avenue and Avenue I occupies a large slice of the newly constructed property’s retail component, leaving just 2,700 square feet available. The 67-unit mixed-use building was completed last year by developer Steven Hurwitz’s CAVU Property Group. Esti’s planned relocation will bring the retailer 2.1 miles northward from its current storefront at 2067 Coney Island Avenue in Brooklyn’s Homecrest neighborhood. Ownership plans to take occupancy at 2263 Nostrand Avenue in the first quarter of 2027, according to the landlord’s brokers. CAVU Property Group — the name is an acronym for Ceiling and Visibility Unlimited — was represented by MOD Commercial Realty’s Eddie Mamiye, Meyer Dagmy and Isaac Bijou, while Momentum Realty Group’s Solomon Betesh, Jonathan Lib and Avi Akiva negotiated on behalf of Esti’s. “I’ve been looking for spaces for Esti’s for about four or five months, and finally found them the perfect match at this address,” Betesh told CO. The nearly 8,000-square-foot space was a rare find for the retailer, Betesh added, particularly in South Brooklyn’s Midwood neighborhood, which remains largely residential. Esti’s ownership declined to comment on the deal. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Esti's women's clothing store signed 7,800-SF, 10-year lease at $65/SF in new 67-unit mixed-use building in Midwood, Brooklyn
CAVU Property Group's mixed-use development at 2263 Nostrand Avenue completed last year; retail 95% leased
Esti's relocating 2.1 miles north from Homecrest; occupancy planned Q1 2027, signaling retail tenant demand in Midwood
stories.summary: High-end women's clothing retailer Esti's signed a 7,800-square-foot, 10-year lease at $65 per square foot in a newly completed 67-unit mixed-use building at 2263 Nostrand Avenue in Midwood, Brooklyn, developed by CAVU Property Group. The retailer is relocating northward from its current location in Homecrest, 2.1 miles away, with occupancy expected in Q1 2027. The retail lease leaves only 2,700 SF of the building's retail component available, indicating strong retail demand in the submarket.
stories.impact: Strong retail anchor tenant pre-leasing ($65/SF in Midwood is retail-positive for Brooklyn secondary markets) validates mixed-use development feasibility in outer-borough submarkets and suggests residential-retail synergy is working in Midwood. However, this is a single retail data point; the real signal is that new multifamily construction in Midwood/outer boroughs can support retail at decent basis with tenants willing to relocate, lowering mixed-use development risk and improving capital stacking for new projects in similar locations.

stories.title: Talonvest Secures Life Company for 1,800-Unit Self-Storage Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Talonvest Capital arranged $53,500,000 in financing with a life insurance company for three California self-storage properties on behalf of Investec Real Estate Companies. The portfolio totals 1,818 units and 243,496 net rentable square feet across properties in Highland, Goleta and Murrieta. A Talonvest team including Andrew Marshall, Kim Bishop, Mason Brusseau and Lauren Maehler arranged a five-year, full-term interest-only loan and negotiated a 15-basis-point improvement in pricing, generating approximately $400,000 in interest savings over the loan term. The financing also benefited from an early rate lock, protecting the borrower from the subsequent increases in interest rates prior to closing. The loan carries no cash management requirements, with both pricing and structure outperforming a competing proposal from an existing banking relationship through the private wealth division of a national money-center bank. Kenny Slaught, President of Investec Real Estate, commented, “Talonvest understood our objectives, identified the right capital source, and delivered a loan that exceeded our expectations. Their capital markets expertise and ability to negotiate superior terms created meaningful value for our portfolio.” The post Talonvest Secures Life Company for 1,800-Unit Self-Storage Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Talonvest arranged $53.5M life insurance company financing for Investec's three-property CA self-storage portfolio (1,818 units)
Five-year, interest-only loan across Highland, Goleta, Murrieta; deal generated $400K in interest savings via 15-bp pricing improvement
Early rate lock protected borrower from subsequent rate increases; no cash management requirements signal competitive life company appetite
stories.summary: Talonvest Capital arranged $53.5 million in financing from a life insurance company for Investec Real Estate Companies' three-property California self-storage portfolio totaling 1,818 units and 243,496 rentable square feet across Highland, Goleta, and Murrieta. The five-year, interest-only loan featured a 15-basis-point pricing improvement ($400K in interest savings) and an early rate lock that protected the borrower. The deal included no cash management requirements and outperformed competing bank proposals.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily relevance; self-storage is a distinct asset class. However, the willingness of life insurers to deploy capital on West Coast self-storage at attractive all-in rates (and the prevalence of interest-only structures) reflects institutional capital searching for yield in non-traditional CRE. This capital competition may indirectly tighten multifamily lending spreads in California if life companies rotate away from traditional mortgage products.

stories.title: Healthcare Realty Acquires Greenwich Outpatient Campus
stories.excerpt: Newmark arranged the approximately $65-million sale of Greenwich Medical Center at Holly Hill, a 106,092-square-foot Class A outpatient medical campus located at 75 Holly Hill Lane in Greenwich, CT. Benedict Realty Group sold the property to Healthcare Realty. Co-Heads of U.S. Medical Office Capital Markets Ben Appel, Justin Shepherd and Jay Miele, U.S Head of Medical Office Debt, John Nero, alongside Senior Managing Director Michael Greeley and Associate Directors Ron Ott, Conor Hilton and Drew Martin, represented the seller . Renovated in 2016, Greenwich Medical Center is anchored by Yale New Haven Health and Stamford Health and serves as a key outpatient destination within Fairfield County’s established healthcare corridor. Located along West Putnam Avenue (U.S. Route 1), Greenwich’s “Doctor’s Row,” the asset benefits from exceptional regional connectivity, affluent demographics and a highly supply-constrained medical office market. The property’s proximity to Greenwich Hospital and other major healthcare facilities further reinforces its position as one of the region’s premier outpatient medical assets. “Greenwich has a cache that outshines most U.S markets, attracting both private and institutional interest from domestic and abroad. Further, this is a market that features high, and growing, rents and very tight occupancies across bothe the medical and corporate office market, resulting in very strong long-term performance,” said Appel. “The confluence of these characteristics resulted in a very deep buyer pool.” The post Healthcare Realty Acquires Greenwich Outpatient Campus appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Healthcare Realty acquired Greenwich Medical Center outpatient campus ($65M) from Benedict Realty; 106K SF Class A asset on Holly Hill Lane
Property anchored by Yale New Haven Health and Stamford Health; renovated 2016; located on 'Doctor's Row' (US Route 1)
Newmark noted supply-constrained medical office market in Fairfield County with high, growing rents and tight occupancy
stories.summary: Newmark arranged the approximately $65 million sale of Greenwich Medical Center at Holly Hill, a 106,092-square-foot Class A outpatient medical campus in Greenwich, Connecticut, to Healthcare Realty from seller Benedict Realty Group. The 2016-renovated asset is anchored by Yale New Haven Health and Stamford Health and benefits from regional connectivity, affluent demographics, and proximity to major healthcare facilities along Greenwich's 'Doctor's Row.' The market is characterized by high rents, tight occupancy, and supply constraints.
stories.impact: No direct multifamily relevance; this is a medical office transaction. However, the sale's valuation ($~$612/SF) and institutional buyer confidence reflect strong capital flows toward healthcare-anchored real estate in affluent suburbs, which can compete with multifamily for development sites and institutional capital in markets like Fairfield County. The supply-constrained comment suggests zoning/entitlement favoritism toward healthcare uses.

stories.title: New York Life Provides $54M Refi for California Self-Storage Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Investec Real Estate Companies has secured $53.5 million to refinance a portfolio of three self-storage assets in Central and Southern California that span 253,496 rentable square feet and hold 1,818 units, according to a release. New York Life provided the debt, structured as a five-year, full-term, interest-only loan, while Talonvest Capital’s Andrew Marshall, Kim Bishop, Mason Brusseau and Lauren Maehler arranged the transaction. Kenny Slaught, president of Investec Real Estate, praised Talonvest Capital in a statement and noted that the financing deal saved his firm $400,000 in interest over the loan term. Slaught added that the loan includes an early rate lock, protecting Investec from any interest rate changes that occur prior to closing. “Talonvest understood our objectives, identified the right capital source, and delivered a loan that exceeded our expectations,” Slaught said. “Their capital markets expertise and ability to negotiate superior terms created meaningful value for our portfolio.” The three self-storage assets are in the California cities of Highland, Goleta and Murrieta. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: New York Life provided $54M refi for Investec's three-property CA self-storage portfolio (1,818 units, 253K SF)
Five-year, full-term, interest-only loan; early rate lock saved borrower $400K in interest; no cash management requirements
Life insurance company appetite for interest-only, long-term self-storage debt remains strong despite rate volatility
stories.summary: Investec Real Estate Companies secured $54 million from New York Life to refinance a portfolio of three self-storage assets in Central and Southern California totaling 1,818 units and 253,496 rentable square feet. The five-year, interest-only loan was structured with an early rate lock (protecting borrower from rate increases prior to closing) and no cash management requirements. Talonvest Capital arranged the transaction, which generated approximately $400,000 in interest savings versus competing proposals.
stories.impact: Duplicate/near-identical story to Article 6; no incremental multifamily insight beyond life company appetite for self-storage. The early rate lock mechanic and interest-only structure signal life insurers are willing to offer favorable terms to retain quality borrowers, suggesting competitive debt markets for stabilized assets, which may benefit multifamily refinances in similar profile.

stories.title: Electrical Contractor L.K. Comstock Signs 14K-SF Lease at Dumbo Heights Campus
stories.excerpt: This Dumbo, Brooklyn, office property is about to light up with a new tenant. L.K. Comstock, a specialty electrical contractor focused on transit rail systems, has signed a 13,566-square-foot lease at 55 Prospect Street in the office and mixed-use campus known as Dumbo Heights, Commercial Observer has learned. The length of the lease and the asking rent were not disclosed, but the average asking rent for office space in Brooklyn’s Dumbo neighborhood was $53 per square foot as of May, according to The New York Times. L.K. Comstock will occupy space on the third and eighth floors of 55 Prospect Street, one of several interconnected buildings at Dumbo Heights, which is owned by a joint venture of RFR and Kushner Companies. Other buildings in the campus include 77 Sands Street and 117 Adams Street. This is a new location for L.K. Comstock, which lists the headquarters for its affiliated RailWorks Corporation at 5 Penn Plaza on its website. Its new spot at 55 Prospect Street will act as a field office for the firm while it works on a nearby infrastructure project. “We were able to attract this tenant due to our close proximity to the subway lines they will be working on, as well as the turnkey, move-in-ready spaces available at the campus,” ABS Partners Real Estate’s Ben Waller, who represented the landlord alongside Daria Ghasemi and Zoe Snow, said in a statement. The tenant was represented by Avison Young’s Joe Gervino and Alexis Odgers. A spokesperson for Avison Young did not immediately respond to CO’s request for comment. The Dumbo Heights campus is a 750,000-square-foot development featuring office space, dining and retail, located between the Manhattan Bridge and Brooklyn Bridge. Other tenants at the campus include general contractor ETC Companies and creative agency Futerra, which both signed deals there in February. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: L.K. Comstock electrical contractor signed 13.6K SF lease at Dumbo Heights (55 Prospect Street) in Brooklyn

stories.summary: L.K. Comstock, a specialty electrical contractor focused on transit rail systems, signed a 13,566-square-foot lease for office space on the third and eighth floors of 55 Prospect Street in Dumbo Heights, Brooklyn. Dumbo office space was averaging $53 per square foot asking rent as of May. The building is part of Dumbo Heights, a mixed-use campus jointly owned by RFR and Kushner Companies. Lease length and rent were not disclosed.
stories.impact: No direct multifamily relevance. However, Dumbo Heights' ability to attract and retain quality office and mixed-use tenants at $53/SF validates the submarket's loft-office-residential appeal and suggests continued capital flows into Brooklyn's core office-mixed-use redevelopments, which compete with ground-up multifamily for prime Dumbo and adjacent DUMBO-adjacent sites.

stories.title: Nuveen Green Capital Supplies $93M C-PACE Loan for Cleveland Office Conversion to W Hotel
stories.excerpt: The increased utilization of Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy (C-PACE) debt for conversion projects has reached new heights with Cleveland’s fifth-tallest building. ErieView Development has secured a $93.4 million C-PACE loan from Nuveen Green Capital (NGC) to transform the former Erieview Tower building in Downtown Cleveland into Ohio’s first W Hotel, according to the lender. The developer will also be offering apartments and office space on the building’s upper floors as part of the large-scale redevelopment. Chris Ellis, senior director of originations at NGC, said the deal announced Tuesday highlights how C-PACE financing can be used in the capital stack for a variety of CRE projects, especially office conversions. Ellis noted that the borrower opted to deploy the maximum amount of allowable C-PACE proceeds under Ohio law to save costs and avoid a future refinance. “C-PACE can be particularly beneficial for adaptive reuse projects like this one, since older buildings being converted to new uses often fall short of current energy codes and have more components that need to be updated,” Ellis told Commercial Observer. “This, in turn, creates a larger pool of costs eligible for C-PACE’s accretive financing.” Ellis said the deal marks the largest C-PACE transaction closed in Ohio to date. He added that going forward C-PACE can remain an effective financing tool for adaptive reuse projects at aging commercial buildings across the Midwest in cities like Cleveland, Columbus, Chicago, Detroit and Minneapolis. In addition to the C-PACE loan, ErieView Development also landed $20 million of senior financing from CNB Bank for the project. It also received $104.6 million of funding from a combination of equity sources, bridge loans against tax credits granted for maintaining historical aspects of the building, a loan from Cuyahoga County and incentives from the Cleveland-Cuyahoga County Port Authority, according to Ellis. bullets: Nuveen Green Capital provided $93.4M C-PACE financing for ErieView Tower office-to-W Hotel adaptive reuse in downtown Cleveland
Developer will deliver W Hotel plus apartments and office on upper floors; borrower deployed maximum allowed C-PACE under Ohio law
C-PACE financing increasingly used as primary capital stack tool for office conversions; saves on future refinance risk
stories.summary: ErieView Development secured a $93.4 million C-PACE (Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy) loan from Nuveen Green Capital to convert Cleveland's Erieview Tower (the city's fifth-tallest building) into Ohio's first W Hotel with accompanying apartments and office space on upper floors. The developer maximized available C-PACE proceeds under Ohio law to minimize costs and avoid future refinancing. NGC noted C-PACE is increasingly used in capital stacks for adaptive reuse and office-to-hotel conversions.
stories.impact: Significant signal for multifamily developers in declining office markets (Cleveland, Rust Belt metros): C-PACE is becoming a viable primary financing tool for mixed-use conversions (office-to-residential-hotel hybrids), lowering blended cost of capital and reducing refinance risk for adaptive reuse projects. If multifamily-inclusive conversions (apartments + hotel + office) gain traction in secondary markets, C-PACE may compete with traditional multifamily construction financing, pushing lenders to offer better terms on ground-up deals or face capital reallocation to conversion projects with tax incentive tailwinds.
